chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: Musicianship in Mutt's band: Mutt, L.Z. Cooper, Alex Hill, Parker Berry
summary: Mutt read at Joe's level, while Cooper, Charlie Moseley and Alex Hill were strong readers and arrangers; Hill and Berry came out with Speed Webb's band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, the two instrumentals, "Ory's Creole Trombone" and (what's the other one...?) "Crooked Blues," I think it is... "Ory's Creole Trombone" is pretty much as they played it all through, even through the revival days, whenever Ory could make it. But the other one, "Crooked Blues," is very sort of orchestrated, and it sounds very much different from, like, the Joe Oliver records of the time, which are much more head stuff, you know. What I'm getting at is, you hadn't worked with Ory up to this time, but you had worked with Mutt. Was Mutt much of a musician technically?

He... Not really. Mutt was about at that time reading in the class that I was. Now, L.Z. Cooper could read pretty good, and this Charlie Moseley, the sax-tenor man that was with us, was an excellent musician. And so far as Alex Hill, he was one of the top arrangers.
I was going to say, he was one of the top musicians.
He had arrangements of his bands. So was Parker Berry. Parker Berry and Alex Hill originally came

out here with a band called Speed Webb, a band out of Ohio. It was a heck of a good band. It was a reading band. All of the guys... Also a trumpet player that played with Andy Kirk when we went on the boat, when I left here on went on a boat -- Earl Thompson was his name; terrific trumpet player.
